liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (3 reviews): Transition from Uncle John's Band into Estimated is called fantastic, Swiss-watch tight, and reportedly never repeated; Transition from Uncle John's Band to Estimated is abrupt yet smooth [17][21][22]
- **Peggy-O** (2 reviews): Played much slower than other 1980s versions of the song; Short but deeply emotional solo; Brent follows Jerry note for note, and Jerry sounds tearful at 'sweet William' [12][18]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Short version with only about a ten-second intro before Jerry sings; Brent contributes some good licks [12]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Reviewer argues this version belongs in a discussion of the all-time top ten [19]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw, Peggy-O and Dear Mr. Fantasy are placed in the top-20 discussion for their songs [19]
- The transition from Playin' into Uncle John's Band is praised as awesome [12]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd87-12-27 t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-12-27 t02 Touch Of Grey**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-12-27 t03 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-12-27 t04 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-12-27 t05 Walkin' Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-12-27 t06 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-12-27 t07 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **gd87-12-27 t08 Big River**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-12-27.141883.fob.schoeps.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 165 min [1]
- **gd87-12-27.sbd.miller.15082.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 159 min; rated 4.67/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Described as an excellent soundboard recording [16]
- **gd1987-12-27.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.85592.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 157 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [3]. Said about its sound: Levels begin very low but are fixed quickly [3]
- **gd1987-12-27.163786.ultramatrix.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: soundboard; 21 songs; 157 min [5]. Said about its sound: Mix and sound fluctuate during roughly the first minute of Touch Of Grey [5]
- **gd1987-12-27.nak300.holtz.lmpp.97960.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 153 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [8]. Said about its sound: Nakamichi 300 recording sounds real nice [21]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first west coast show and first New Year's run; this night opened it [11]
- Reviewer attended all four shows of the run; this was the first of four [13]
- Reviewer's first New Year's run out west; stayed near Palo Alto and at a Super 8 near the arena [16]
- Reviewer attended all four nights; it was their first Bay Area show and only New Year's run [17]
- Reviewer's first Bay Area show, remembered fondly [18]
- Reviewer's first New Year's run as a California resident, living in San Francisco [21]
- Bill Graham appeared at midnight on a scale model of the Golden Gate Bridge [22]
- Ken Kesey did a skit during set break, and Mason Williams played Classical Gas live [22]
- Reviewer found the second set solid and better than the Worcester or Hampton shows from that spring [11]
- Seen as a good, solid opening to the New Year's run, but nothing mind-blowing [16]
- Reviewer ranks the show among the top three, behind only Madison 9/18 and Kingswood 6/30 [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-12-27.141883.fob.schoeps.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Source Info: (FOB) Audience > unknown Schoeps mics > PCM; Transfer Info: PCM (Sony SL-10)> Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 (wav… [1]. Also: A 16-second patch in Touch Of Grey comes from the Nakamichi 300 source, shnid 97960 [1]
- **gd87-12-27.sbd.miller.15082.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> Cm -> Dat (Tascam DA20) -> CD (Tascam CDRW700) -> EAC -> SHN via Charlie Miller [2]
- **gd1987-12-27.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.85592.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) D [3]. Also: Two different soundboard cassette masters were combined seamlessly; tapes came from Paul Scotton and Joani Walker [3]
- **gd1987-12-27.163786.ultramatrix.walker.scotton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Joani Walker's Master Ultramatrix Soundboard Cassettes (TDK MA-XG90) [5]. Also: Made from master cassettes from Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, transferred by Charlie Miller; multiple masters were used [5]
- **gd1987-12-27.nak300.holtz.lmpp.97960.flac16**: taped by Greg Holtz; transferred by Brian Green and  Evan K.; source: Nakamichi CM-300's with CP-4 shotgun capsules > Sony D-5 cassette recorder > MAC [8]
